summary.tldr: Expands border, immigration, policing, mail, and anti-money laundering powers, and changes rules for sharing and collecting information.
what_it_does: Gives the Canada Border Services Agency free facilities for work under the Customs Act and access, at certain locations, to goods headed for export.
Creates a temporary faster path for the Health Minister to add precursor chemicals to Schedule V under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act.
Changes Canada Post rules so items in the mail can be seized, detained, or kept only under an Act of Parliament, and lets Canada Post open letters in certain cases.

Changes coast guard, immigration, and refugee rules, including more information sharing, ending the designated countries of origin regime, and adding new grounds that can make a refugee claim ineligible.
Raises penalties and changes compliance rules under anti-money laundering law, requires more entities to enrol with FINTRAC, bars some large cash dealings, and adds more information-sharing powers.
Updates investigation and data access rules for police and CSIS, creates a framework for authorised access to information, and changes sex offender reporting and information-sharing rules.
summary.background: It was introduced in the House of Commons on 3 June 2025.
